# Http

**PPL language/runtime 4.00 - host object.**

[Object model and calling conventions](../objects.md) | [API index](index.md)

Static entry point for policy-controlled HTTP requests and downloads.

[Behavior, constraints and examples](../../../new_ppl.md#http-objects-400).

## Download

```PPL
Http.Download(STRING url, STRING file) HttpResponse
```

Static function.

Streams a successful GET response to a temporary board-relative file and commits it atomically only after completion. The configured response-size limit applies; failures leave the destination unchanged and return an invalid response.

## FormDecode

```PPL
Http.FormDecode(STRING text) STRING
```

Static function.

Decodes one `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` field, treating `+` as a space. Byte sequences that are not valid UTF-8 are replaced rather than reported.

## FormEncode

```PPL
Http.FormEncode(STRING text) STRING
```

Static function.

Encodes one `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` field, where a space is `+`. `SetForm()` already applies this encoding automatically.

## Get

```PPL
Http.Get(STRING url) HttpResponse
```

Static function.

Performs a policy-controlled GET request and returns an `HTTPRESPONSE`. Transport or policy failures return an invalid response and report details through `Error.Last()`; HTTP error statuses remain valid responses.

## New

```PPL
Http.New(HttpMethod method, STRING url) HttpRequest
```

Static function.

Creates a mutable `HTTPREQUEST` for `HttpMethod.Get`, `Head` or `Post` and the supplied URL. It performs no network I/O until `Send()` is called.

## UrlDecode

```PPL
Http.UrlDecode(STRING text) STRING
```

Static function.

Decodes one RFC 3986 URL component. A `+` remains literal; byte sequences that are not valid UTF-8 are replaced rather than reported.

## UrlEncode

```PPL
Http.UrlEncode(STRING text) STRING
```

Static function.

Percent-encodes one URL component using RFC 3986 rules, where a space is `%20` and `+` is encoded. Encode single values only, never a whole `name=value&...` string, because separators must stay unencoded.
